newsitem.title: UK: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON MEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-PEN PICTURES OF WIMBLEDON MEN'S SEMIFINALISTS.

text.p: singles semifinalists at Wimbledon on Friday:

PETE SAMPRAS (U.S.) ATP ranking 1, seeded 1. Age 25, height 1.85m. Grand Slam victories 9: Australian Open 1994 1997, Wimbledon 1993 1994 1995, U.S. Open 1990 1993 1995 1996. The man to beat at Wimbledon, a consummate all-round athlete who can play every shot. Fierce serve and volleyer, although serve has been off-key recently and he was beaten in third round of French Open and in quarter-finals at Queen's Club. However, has had an excellent Wimbledon, culminating in the quarter-final defeat of Boris Becker, a loss which brought on the announcement of the German's retirement from major tournaments. Sampras began playing tennis at age of seven and became youngest U.S. Open winner aged 19 years 28 days. Coached by Paul Annacone since Tim Gullikson, his coach and mentor, became ill and died last year.
TODD WOODBRIDGE (Australia) - ATP singles ranking 37. ATP doubles ranking 1. Age 26. Height 1.78 m Weight 71 kg. Grand Slam victories: None.

Reaching the semifinals here surpasses his previous Grand Slam performances the best of which was reaching the fourth round at the Australian Open (1991). Surprise semifinalist who was not expected to get past the first round against number five seed and world number two Michael Chang. But he succeeded after five sets and three hours 55 minutes play -- the longest first round match. Got through the next two rounds in straight sets before taking four to dispense with number 12 seed Pat Rafter. He is least favourite to win this year's Wimbledon ranked at 16-1 by bookmakers William Hill. Holds just two career singles titles: 1997 Adelaide where he defeated compatriot Scott Draper and 1995 Coral Springs where he beat Briton Greg Rusedksi. He and partner Mark Woodforde are ranked number one in the world and dominate men's doubles. The pair have won eight career Grand Slam doubles including consecutive Wimbledon titles (1994-1996).
MICHAEL STICH (Germany) - ATP singles ranking 88. Age 28. Height 1.94 m Weight 79 kg. Grand Slam victories: Wimbledon (1991).

His final Wimbledon before retiring later this year, a relaxed Stich has dropped just two sets here. Beat British number one Tim Henman in quarter-finals. Went out in last year's tournament to eventual winner Richard Krajicek after disastrous first round exits in 1995 and 1994. Beat Boris Becker in 1991 in all-German final. Fell to Yegveny Kafelnikov in 1996 Roland Garros. In 1994 was runner-up in the French Open to Andre Agassi.
CEDRIC PIOLINE (France) ATP ranking 44, unseeded, age 28, height 1.88m, weight 79kg. Best Grand Slam result - finalist at U.S. Open 1993.

A talented player with an all-round game and a punishing return. But he can be temperamental and his career has been a series of peaks and troughs. Reached number nine in the world in January 1994. Member of France's Davis Cup winning team last December. Feels comfortable on grass and has reached the Wimbledon quarter-finals three times. Was beaten by Pete Sampras in straight sets at U.S. Open final in 1993. Mother was a member of Romanian world championship volleyball team and father was also a top volleyball player. He is married to Mireille Bercot and has a four-year-old son.
